summary.intent: Use the GSD manager workflow to drive milestone v2.0 closeout across cipher-box: refresh the phase dashboard, verify Phase 70.1 via UAT, fix a mis-flagged Phase 69 status, then discuss/plan/execute the remaining unblocked phases (74-79), continuing autonomously across quota resets via scheduled cron resumes.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 was verified (SC#6 crash-resume suite passed 6/6 after restarting the API from source), Phase 69's false 'partial' status was root-caused to a plan-file scanner bug and fixed, both were merged to main via PR #606. Phases 74 and 75 were fully planned, executed, and verified (74 code-verified with only CI-gated legs remaining; 75 fully verified and marked complete) on their own feat branches; Phase 77 was mid-execution (plans committed, plan-checker not yet run) when the transcript ends, with 76/78/79 still queued.

repo: gsd-core's plan-file scanner (`plan-scan.cjs:28`) has a loose `/PLAN/i` substring fallback that miscounts any `.md` file merely containing 'PLAN' (e.g. `69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md`) as an extra plan, causing false `partial`/'Executing' dashboard status even when a phase is 100% done.
The manager dashboard's `is_active` flag just means 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not that an agent is actually running.

`phase uat-passed --require-verification` treats 'implementation complete + verification passed but no UAT file' as not-fully-done, downgrading disk_status to `partial` (relevant for phases verified only via CI/cargo, not conversational UAT).

vitest does not load `.env` files — sdk-e2e test harness falls back to a default test secret unless `SDK_E2E_SECRET` is explicitly exported, causing 401s against the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` even when `.env` files are aligned.

The live API on :3000 can silently be a stale `node dist/main.js` process (detached, PPID 1) serving old compiled code instead of current source — must verify PID/start-time before trusting test results against it.

Claude Code sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot `EnterWorktree` into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree' error) — parallel worktree-isolated background planning across multiple agents is a dead end in this environment.
`commit.gpgsign=false` in this repo means commits don't block on 1Password biometric prompts, which matters for autonomous/unattended runs.

Pre-commit hooks in this monorepo (lint-staged) are slow (~1-2 min) and can make commits look hung when they actually landed; the gsd commit helper sometimes false-negatives `commit_failed` even though the commit succeeded.

code.finding: Loose fallback matcher counts any .md filename containing substring 'PLAN' (case-insensitive) as a plan file if it's not a -SUMMARY.md, causing false positives like 'WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md'.
is_active is computed purely from 'file modified in phase dir within last 5 minutes', not from actual agent liveness.

workflow: When a background agent dies mid-task from a session/quota limit, check disk state directly (git log, ls PLAN files, VERIFICATION status) rather than trusting the agent's last reported message — actual progress is often further along than the failure notification implies.

Sequential processing on the main checkout (switching branches per phase) is more robust than parallel worktree-isolated background agents for phases whose commands (pnpm/cargo) require the installed workspace.

When scheduling autonomous resume-after-quota-reset work via cron, the resume prompt must be corrected/updated if the working method changes mid-session (stale instructions pointing at removed worktrees caused a wasted cycle) — always delete and recreate the cron with current state.

For infra-gated verification legs (e.g. Windows-only compile, multi-platform e2e matrix) that can't run on the current host, record them in the phase's UAT.md/STATE.md as infra-gated rather than treating the phase as blocked on human verification.

friction: Three background planners (74, 75, 77) died simultaneously mid-run due to hitting the session/quota limit, requiring disk-state reassessment and relaunch.
EnterWorktree failed for sub-agents launched from repo root trying to pin into an existing worktree, wasting a launch cycle before pivoting to sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch approach.

A Phase 75 sub-agent stopped itself early (~21 min) due to a flawed self-made background-wait loop, not an actual quota limit, requiring detection and relaunch with explicit 'no background-wait' instructions.
Phase 77's planner produced 10 plans but the commit didn't land before the 09:40 quota cutoff, leaving them uncommitted and requiring manual recovery/commit on resume.
A misleading rustc E0277 diagnostic (anchored to stdlib, not actual repo code) needed a manual `cargo check --workspace` to rule out as a real regression before trusting Phase 75 as complete.
`.env` grep was denied by the user/permission system as a secret file, requiring a workaround of reading only package.json scripts instead.
open_items: Phase 77 (crypto hygiene/terminology cleanup): 10 plans committed but plan-checker had not yet run and execution had not started when the transcript ends.
Phases 76, 78, 79 still need discuss/plan/execute — none is expected to need discuss-phase but that's unconfirmed.

Phase 74's two CI-gated verification legs (Windows compile of WinFsp code, 3-platform desktop-e2e matrix) remain unverified locally — need CI confirmation before `/gsd-verify-work 74` can close it out.
None of the feat branches (74, 75, 77+) have been pushed/opened as PRs yet per user's no-auto-merge/no-auto-PR instruction — all awaiting user review.
A safety-net cron resume was scheduled for ~09:50 (and possibly needs another one for the next ~5h quota window) to keep autonomous closeout going for 76/78/79.
